notes: Kits get their own page · User groups: a category tree, and products one by one · The same category name under two parents

entries.title: Kits get their own page
items: A customer's Catalog menu now has Categories, SKUs and Kits. Kits lists the products built from other SKUs, with New kit; the SKU list keeps everything else, kit parts included.
The design studio's "Catalog page" step is now "Shop page", the name buyers see on the portal.

entries.title: User groups: a category tree, and products one by one
items: "Only these categories" shows every level as a tree. Tick a category and everything under it comes with it — its sub-categories show as "included". Before, a ticked parent didn't bring its sub-categories' products.
New on a group's Catalog tab: Products, one by one. Find a product and choose Always show (an extra SKU this group wouldn't otherwise see) or Always hide.

entries.title: The same category name under two parents
items: Skincare > Sale and Gifts > Sale can now both exist — a name only has to be unique among the categories beside it. Adding a second "Sale" under the same parent says so plainly.
The SKU import's categories column takes paths: "Makeup > Lipsticks" files the product there, making any level that's missing.
The reorganizer's spreadsheet writes each category as its path, and reads paths back, so two categories with the same name never get mixed up.

entries.title: Security update
items: A library Amphora uses to check what's sent to it is updated, closing a way an oversized request could use up the server's memory. Nothing changes on screen.

entries.title: Categories at every level, and a merge that keeps user groups
items: The Categories card shows the whole tree — sub-categories of sub-categories included. Before, anything deeper than two levels was hidden from the card even though it existed.
Add a sub-category straight from the card: pick where it goes (Top level, or Under a category) next to the name, then Add.

Reorganize the catalog checks each change the moment you add it, so Apply is always one click ("Apply 2 changes"). Reshape the tree nests at any depth — drop a category onto another to put it under that one.

Merging a category into one of its own sub-categories now works: the kept one takes its place. User groups limited to "Only these categories", and their allowances, follow a merge or delete too, and Undo puts them back.
"view SKUs" and each category's SKU count open this customer's own SKU list, filtered to that category and everything under it. The SKU list has a category filter of its own.

entries.title: The design studio previews every setting before you publish
items: Featured products, the Orders page's opening tab, related products, low-stock-first, labels on the reports, accounting and bulk pages, and the approvals ship-to all change in the preview as you set them. Before, these only showed after Publish.
Buyers still see the published portal until you press Publish. The draft is yours alone — another designer previewing the same portal sees their own.

entries.title: The menu stays where you left it
items: Clicking an item low in the side menu no longer throws the menu back to the top: the menu stays put while the page scrolls, and so does a customer's own menu.
Fold any menu group you don't use by clicking its heading. This device remembers what you folded; the group holding the page you're on always stays open.

entries.title: Pick runs walk pick priority 1 first
items: The pick slip and the scan station now send pickers to locations in pick-priority order — priority 1, then 2, then 3 — before anything without a priority, which follows the walk path as before. Amphora already took the right quantities from each location; it listed the stops in walk order, so a priority-3 shelf could come first on the slip.
The slip's ROUTE line now reads "pick priority first, then walk-path order".

entries.title: Find a location by typing it when receiving a pallet
items: Location on the Receive desk's Pallet mode is now a search box: type or scan part of a code and the list narrows to match. Leave it blank to land the pallet on the dock, as before.
Location lists everywhere are in aisle order — MAIN46-B-6-5 now comes before MAIN46-B-46-1 instead of after it.

entries.title: Portal typefaces ship with Amphora
items: The typefaces a portal theme can choose now come inside Amphora itself instead of being fetched from Google when Amphora is built — nothing changes on screen, and portals never load fonts from Google.

entries.title: Security update
items: Amphora now runs on a patched version of its web framework, closing a critical issue in image handling and a way to slow the server down. Nothing changes on screen; update when you can.

entries.title: Kits ordered report
items: Reports → Kits ordered: how many of each kit got ordered over a date range — prebuilt kits, build-a-kits and kits an upstream system sent as parts — with the number of orders and the last time each was ordered. Filter by customer, kit type and dates; download as CSV. Cancelled orders are left out.

Every order now records its kits as it's placed, so build-a-kits count right even though they arrive as their parts. Orders placed before this update are filled in from their own records the first time the report runs.
Brands see the same in their portal: Reports → Usage → By kit. The report builder has a Kits ordered subject and a ready-to-run starter.

entries.title: Which services and countries each user group may ship to
items: Customer → Client portal → User groups → Shipping: under the carriers, Services this group may pick — e.g. only admins get overnight. Nothing checked keeps every service the customer allows; a group can narrow, never widen.

Countries: Anywhere (the default — existing groups don't change), US only (territories included), or Only these countries. Checkout says so under Ship to before the order is placed; address-book and fixed group addresses are checked too.
Fixed: a portal order's shipping service is now checked against what the group may pick on every route — checkout, bulk, saved carts and the portal API — not only its carrier.

entries.title: Ask AI for a portal theme from the brand guidelines
items: After the Design studio reads a brand's guidelines PDF, Ask AI for a theme suggests which colour does what, a font pairing, corners and button style, with its reasons. It only sees what was read from the PDF and may only use the guide's own colours; text that wouldn't read is fixed and every correction is shown. You still choose, Apply to the preview and Publish.
Off until switched on: Settings → Integrations → AI assistant → Portal theme from brand guidelines.
Easier to find: the Your brand section and the colors step say you can start from the guidelines, and a card points to it until the brand's colours are set.

entries.title: SKUs: find the kits, clearer imports and price breaks
items: Both SKU lists have a Type filter — Kits, Stocked, Print on demand, Service. Export CSV and Placards follow it.

"Which spreadsheet do I use?" beside the customer's imports: Import CSV makes the products; Kit contents, Price breaks, Ordering limits and Lots each set one thing on SKUs that already exist and replace that SKU's list.
The SKU import says barcode columns are for the warehouse — scanning and placards — and never show in a portal.
Price breaks read "$ off each unit" / "% off each unit" and every row shows what it comes to, e.g. "= $64.00 each at 24+".

entries.title: Practice in the demo world
items: Practice (demo world only): six guided exercises a trainer hands a new hire — receive a truck with a short line, put away, pick and ship an order, count three shelves, process a return, enter an order from a buyer's email.

Start builds a fresh scenario through the real engines; the checklist ticks itself as the work gets done on the real screens, and Try again makes a new one. It never touches the main install's stock. New hires need their own account inside the demo world.

entries.title: Onboarding a brand: welcome pack, Getting started and portal Help
items: Customer → Overview → Welcome pack (PDF) prints a few pages for a new brand in your own branding: their portal address and how to sign in, the ship-by promise and cut-off, carriers, how to send stock in and mark the cartons, reports, and who to ask. Sections that don't apply are left out.

When a brand admin signs in, the portal home shows Getting started — invite your people, groups, approvals, the first order, a scheduled report, low-stock alerts. Each line ticks itself from what has actually happened, links to the screen that does it, and the card can be hidden.
Every portal has a Help page (Help in the account menu): short guides in the brand's own look, showing each person only what they can do, with a search box.

entries.title: Floor cheat sheets: one printed page per station
items: Knowledge base → Floor cheat sheets: eight one-page sheets — scan mode, receiving, putaway, picking, pack & ship, cycle counts, returns and put back — to print, laminate and keep where the work happens.

Each has the steps in big numbered type, What the screen tells you (the messages people actually see, like “may have gone through” or a red DO NOT SHIP placard) and When you're stuck, ending with who to ask. They wear your logo and are generated from this version, so reprint after an update.

entries.title: Learn your job, not the whole manual
items: The knowledge base opens on Your first day as… — a short path for each job (receiving, pick & pack, floor lead, office, billing, setting up, developers): the handful of things that job does every day, each with the screen that does it and the exact section that explains it. Handbook (PDF) prints just that job's pages and articles instead of the whole reference.
A ? in the top bar on every screen opens the help for that screen in a side panel — press ? anywhere outside a field.

New installs: the dashboard opens with Go live, the first-run steps in order (the clock, the building, the team, a customer ready to trade, the first receipt, the first shipment…), each ticked off from the real thing. Hide it, or bring it back from Settings → General.
Reports → Help questions (owners and admins) lists what your team asked the help and didn't find, in their own words — the docs still to write.

The knowledge base's sections are regrouped into eleven, in the order people need them: Start here, Team & security, Customers, Client portals, Catalog, Receiving & stock, Orders & shipping, Billing & reports, Print, mail & compliance, Platform & integrations, Reference.

entries.title: Stock that goes bad moves its orders, files aren't received twice, paid invoices stay paid
items: Marking stock damaged or quarantined, writing it off, destroying it or counting it down now re-reserves the orders that were counting on it — from other lots, earliest expiry first, or backordered — and the screen names the orders that moved. Before, they stayed reserved on stock that couldn't ship.

Mass receiving: the same file received a second time (another screen, a double click, the sheet uploaded again) stops and says when and by whom it was received; Receive it again anyway is there for a genuine second delivery.
Big import checks run in short parts, so the floor keeps scanning while a 6,000-row file is checked — no more “database is locked” on the scanners.
A paid invoice can't be voided any more — correct it with a credit on the next invoice, or a refund.

entries.title: Friendlier error pages — and they know when the Wi-Fi dropped
items: A page that can't load now says so with a bit of warehouse humour (“This page tripped over a pallet.”), what to check (did what you were saving go through?), and Try again, Go back or Home — instead of a bare “This page couldn't load”.
Lost the connection? It says that (“The Wi-Fi went on break.”) and tries again by itself the moment the connection is back.

A real failure shows a short reference code that matches the server's log, for whoever runs Amphora. Pages that don't exist, scan mode and client portals (in the brand's own look) get the same treatment.

entries.title: Idle stock fees: stock that doesn't ship costs more to keep
items: Customer → Billing → Idle stock fees: a storage surcharge for SKUs that haven't shipped in months — by default 50% of the bin or pallet fee at 6 months, 75% at 12, 100% at 18, 150% at 24, each client's own tiers editable.

Idle means no unit shipped: the clock runs from the last shipment (or the first receipt, if it never shipped); receipts and moves don't restart it, shipping one unit does. A location shared with other products counts as a share.
Three modes per client: Inactive (nothing), Draft (alerts only, nothing charged — a dry run) and On (the monthly invoice adds the surcharge, averaged over the days it was On, like storage).

Alerts each morning to the brand's admins and the client's new Account manager, by email, and the Billing team's bell: SKUs coming up on a tier within the warning window (30 days by default) and SKUs that just reached one — each told once.
Reports → Idle stock: by client, every SKU past a tier or coming up — months idle, positions, the surcharge now and at the next tier — with a CSV export.

entries.title: The floor, hammered: lost answers, double taps, counts, returns and billing made safe
items: No answer from the server? The scanner now says it may have gone through, and doing it again is safe — it's sent with the same key, so a receipt, move or pick that already landed is never booked twice. Before, it said “this wasn't saved”, and doing it again booked it twice.

A second Enter from the gun (or a double tap) while a scan is being sent is ignored on the pick and receiving screens; the same stop sent twice in a moment is recorded once. Pallet receipts, return receipts, kitting pulls, Confirm shipped and the print buttons are done once when pressed again after a lost answer.

Pick & pack and Receiving can now finish their own work: confirm put-backs, show up as Being picked by, answer Put back / Keep when an order comes off their cart, release an empty location, and decide what happened to their own refused offline scans. Anything outside a role now says so (“Pick & pack can't do this — ask a manager”) instead of “Authentication required”.

Finish picking waits until every stop is confirmed or recorded short — no more lines shorted silently because a colleague's stop was still on its way — and waits while the office is editing the order. A run where every stop came up short sends the order back to Backordered instead of leaving it at the bench as Packed.

Counts: locations the system believes are empty are listed on the count (and the sheet) and locked with the rest; pallets can't be driven in or out of a counted location; a line sent back for recount must be counted again before it can be approved; two counters who disagree send the line back for a recount; a pick & pack or receiving person can't approve their own count.
Returns can't bring back more than an order shipped, a product it didn't ship, or the same units twice; Undo shipped is refused once a return has brought units back.
Invoices: a draft whose dates overlap another invoice is refused (storage would bill those days twice); Recalculate and Issue can no longer cross and leave fees on an invoice that doesn't show them.

Packing: a box line must be the order line's own product; re-boxing after closing bills (or credits) the difference in cartons; Confirm shipped with open boxes closes them first, weight check and carton fee included; cancelling a packed order takes its boxes off the ship desk (void a bought label first).

Undo a receipt never takes units off the cart or stock open orders have reserved. A cancelled print job puts its unused blanks back on their shelves, and Mark printed pressed at two stations books once. Two people moving one pallet to two places: one moves it, the other is told.
Imports read UTF-16 and older-Excel files correctly, refuse an .xlsx that unpacks past 64 MB, and every CSV Amphora exports opens formulas as text.

entries.title: Username and PIN sign-in for floor people without an email
items: Add a person → Username & PIN (no email): a username like maria.l and a 4–8 digit PIN you set and hand over. They sign in on the same page — the username where the email goes, the PIN where the password goes.

Fenced in on purpose: floor roles only (Warehouse, Pick & pack, Receiving, PPD lead); guessable PINs (1111, 1234) refused; 5 wrong PINs lock it for 15 minutes; no two-factor asked; a username never matches an email account.
Manage on a PIN person: change the username or set a new PIN (signs them out everywhere). No email ever goes to them, and Forgot password? doesn't apply.
The sign-in page now reads Email or username / Password or PIN.

entries.title: Settings → Users rebuilt for a big team, and Forgot password? for staff
items: The Team list: search by name or email, Active / Deactivated / All, filter by role, sort by name, last seen or newest; one compact row per person with role, how they sign in, 2FA and when they were last seen; the first 50, then Show more.
One Manage per person opens everything under the row — role, print shop, new password, deactivate, sign out everywhere, reset 2FA — instead of three buttons on every row.
Add a person and Invite several are buttons at the top; their forms open above the list only when you need them. Add a person has a Generate button for the temporary password.

Invite several reads a whole To: line — addresses separated by spaces, commas or semicolons, with or without names — as one person each. Before, a line of addresses was read as one person and most of them were never checked.
The invite preview is a table, one person per row: the new people first, then those left alone and why, with counts. The form now says up front that each person gets their own temporary password.

Forgot password? on the staff sign-in page: a link by email to choose a new password (works once, lasts an hour, signs every device out; two-factor still applies). It never says whether an address has an account, and single sign-on accounts are pointed to the company's sign-in. No email set up? The page says to ask an admin.

Switched single sign-on off? People who only signed in through it are no longer stuck: Settings → Users lists them (Can't sign in), they can use Forgot password?, or an admin sets a password under Manage. They become password accounts; single sign-on still finds them if you switch it back on.
Dropdowns across the app keep their text clear of the arrow.
